The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 3.8% on October 16, 2026, its eighth straight losing session and its longest run since 2008. The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.5% on the same date, and tech stocks lost more than a trillion dollars in value.

24/7 Wall Street

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) tracks a similar index. It fell 4.14% to $493.39. It closed at $589.45 on October 6, so it is now down about 16% since then and sits about 25% below its 52-week high of $655.95. The fund is still up 64.12% for 2026, so the selloff likely reflects investors repricing the AI spending cycle and unwinding popular positions.

Equipment Makers Fell With Chip Designers

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) fell 5.95%. Intel lost 5.79%, Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) 5.63%, Marvell Technology 5.56% and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) 4.52%. Three chip equipment makers also fell. KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) dropped 5.00%, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) 4.87% and Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) 4.82%.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) slid only 1.43%. Chip designers, memory makers and equipment makers all fell on the same day, which suggests investors doubt the spending cycle that pays all of them.

Short Sellers Have Earned $32B Over The Past Week Amid Chipmaker Selloff: Report
Shashank Nayar

CRWV
^NDX
^GSPC
Trade CRWV on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bearish investors accumulated roughly $32 billion in paper profits over seven days as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped over 12% during an eight-session slump.

Broad market indexes felt the ripple effect, with the S&P 500 on track for its worst weekly decline since June and the Nasdaq 100 sliding 5%.

Short sellers betting against AI cloud provider CoreWeave Inc. netted more than $1 billion in mark-to-market profits following distressed debt signals and rising default risks.

Short sellers have bagged a multi-billion-dollar payday amid a retreat in semiconductor stocks driven by CoreWeave's debt concerns.

Short sellers recorded $32 billion in gross paper profits over a seven-day span as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeted more than 12%, S3 data showed, as quoted by Bloomberg.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

The sector benchmark, widely known as the SOX, extended its slump to eight consecutive trading days on Friday, putting it on pace to mirror its longest losing streak since 2006.

Market Anxiety Around AI Spending Persist

The recent decline reflects growing market anxiety about elevated interest rates, lofty tech valuations, and the massive AI capital expenditures.

The selloff in chips has spilled over into broader equity benchmarks, setting the S&P 500 up for a 1.7% weekly decline, its steepest since June, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropped 5% in the week ending October 16.

Out of the 30 companies comprising the SOX index, 20 have lost over 10% of their value since the downturn began. Coherent Corp.(COHR) led the losses with a dive of nearly 30%.

"The run up in chips was very aggressive so invariably there was going to be some consolidation or pull back," Dec Mullarkey of SLC Management told Bloomberg.

CoreWeave Shorts Yield Massive Returns

Short sellers targeting CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV), an AI-focused cloud computing firm, logged over $1 billion in gains as the company's equity dropped more than 20% over the week.

CoreWeave's debt instruments slipped into distressed territory, with credit-default swaps indicating a greater than 50% likelihood of default over the next five years.S3 data noted that a portion of the short interest in CoreWeave stems from convertible bond arbitrage strategies rather than purely directional bearish bets.

"CoreWeave specifically is going to need a new story," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager of the Rational Equity Armor Fund told Bloomberg. "It's going to need time to digest this new reality."

The Nasdaq 100 (^NDX) is home to some of the biggest success stories in tech and growth investing. However, certain stocks in the index face challenges like profitability concerns, rising costs, or shifts in market trends.

Investing in Nasdaq 100 stocks isn't just about picking big names - it's about finding the right ones, and that's where StockStory comes in. That said, here is one Nasdaq 100 stock that has huge potential and two that may struggle.

Two Stocks to Sell:
NXP Semiconductors (NXPI)

Market Cap: $58.27 billion

Spun off from Dutch electronics giant Philips in 2006, NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ: NXPI) is a designer and manufacturer of chips used in autos, industrial manufacturing, mobile devices, and communications infrastructure.

Why Does NXPI Give Us Pause?

Products and services are facing end-market challenges during this cycle, as seen in its flat sales over the last two years

Anticipated sales growth of 15.7% for the next year implies demand will be shaky

At $226.62 per share, NXP Semiconductors trades at 13.2x forward P/E. To fully understand why you should be careful with NXPI, check out our full research report (it's free).

Marriott (MAR)

Market Cap: $100.6 billion

Founded by J. Willard Marriott in 1927, Marriott International (NASDAQ:MAR) is a global hospitality company with a portfolio of over 7,000 properties and 30 brands, spanning 130+ countries and territories.

Why Are We Bearish on MAR?

Softer revenue per room over the past two years suggests it might have to invest in new amenities such as restaurants and bars to attract customers

Capital intensity will likely increase as its free cash flow margin is anticipated to drop by 1.2 percentage points over the next year

Unchanged returns on capital make it difficult for the company's valuation multiple to re-rate

Marriott is trading at $384.04 per share, or 30.2x forward P/E. Dive into our free research report to see why there are better opportunities than MAR.

One Stock to Watch:
Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX)

Market Cap: $128.9 billion

Founded in 1989 with a mission to create medicines that treat the underlying causes of disease rather than just symptoms, Vertex Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:VRTX) develops and markets transformative medicines for serious diseases, with a focus on cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, and pain management.

Why Does VRTX Catch Our Eye?

Annual revenue growth of 13.5% over the last five years beat the sector average and underscores the unique value of its offerings

Adjusted operating profits increased over the last two years as the company gained some leverage on its fixed costs and became more efficient

Market-beating returns on capital illustrate that management has a knack for investing in profitable ventures

(NASDAQ:META), the parent company of dominant social media platforms, is a multinational technology company that develops products to connect people. On October 15, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) closed at $736.72 per share with a $1.88 trillion market capitalization. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) posted an 11.61% YTD gain, trading within a 52-week range of $520.26 to $779.82.

Wedgewood Partners stated the following regarding Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) was another standout performer in the portfolio this quarter. Revenues grew 28%, and the Company launched a slew of AI products and updates that the market viewed positively. Meta has a long history of launching massive, objectively successful products. Yet the market often ignores them or even penalizes them. While Meta's Metaverse investments are a clear reason to be skeptical that management will bat 1.000, they are hardly a reason to discount every clear and obvious home run, or even grand slam. More recently, the Company's Threads app, launched just 3 years ago, has over 500 million monthly active users. This quarter, Meta also rolled out its Muse Agent, which users can set on autopilot to handle mundane but productive tasks like lowering phone bills or renewing license plate tags. The Muse Agent works in tandem with a private virtual machine (we estimate its value at $500 to $1,000) that every user gets for free and that maintains the user's privacy and security throughout the process.

While it is still early days, the Company's advancements on the LLM frontier, along with its long history of working with encryption, especially through WhatsApp, have made the rollout and execution of Muse Agent among the best since OpenAI launched ChatGPT. Over the next several years, we think Meta has plenty more AI products and investments that will generate returns on par with those of past years."
